project: Weave Self-Iteration Browser Where Contract Tightening
description: Small Ralph self-iteration for branch ralph/self-iteration-20260519-143531. The previous active PRD belonged to ralph/self-iteration-20260519-132647 and all stories were passing, so it was archived under scripts/ralph/archive/self-iteration-20260519-143836/. No PR CI auto-fix context was present in progress.txt. Kickoff health: latest GitHub main CI run 26080216394 completed green on commit 1aa796d while Codespaces prebuild 26080216161 was still in progress; local sampled checks for known fresh-CI risks passed via `go test ./cmd/server -run 'TestBuildEmbeddingProvider|TestEmbeddedWebDist|TestSPA|TestCI'` and `npm --prefix web test -- --run src/components/admin/__tests__/ComplianceReportsPage.test.tsx`. DOG-003 through DOG-005 have committed regression coverage, but code inspection found the Browser structured filter builder still emitting a UI-only array shape for `containsAnyTerm` even though the canonical WhereClause contract is string-based. This PRD focuses on tightening the Browser object exploration WhereClause surface used by upper-layer ObjectSet experiences.

userStories.name: Canonicalize Browser containsAnyTerm filters
userStories.description: Make the Browser structured filter builder emit the canonical backend WhereClause shape for `containsAnyTerm` instead of preserving a UI-only array of terms.
bdd_acceptance: Given the Browser filter builder is set to `contains any term`, When the user enters `OpenAI   Codex` and adds the filter, Then the saved filter value is the string `OpenAI Codex` rather than an array.
Given multiple Browser filters include a `containsAnyTerm` clause, When `buildWhereClause` serializes the request body, Then the clause keeps `value` as a string inside the `and` group.
Given the filter chip renders a canonical `containsAnyTerm` string, When the user reviews the active filter, Then the visible chip value remains readable as `OpenAI Codex`.

userStories.name: Expose range and prefix Where operators in Browser filters
userStories.description: Expand the Browser structured filter controls beyond `eq`, `gt`, `lt`, and text contains so analysts can build backend-supported range and prefix clauses without leaving the object browser.
bdd_acceptance: Given the user selects `gte` or `lte` in the Browser filter builder, When they enter a numeric value, Then the generated WhereClause uses the selected operator with a numeric value.
Given the user selects `startsWith`, When they enter a prefix, Then the generated WhereClause uses `type: "startsWith"` with a string value.

Given a saved search reloads a Browser filter using one of these supported operators, When the filter chip renders, Then it shows the operator label instead of falling back to an unsupported raw token.

userStories.name: Guard Browser sort requests with property metadata
userStories.description: Prevent the Browser table from sending server-side sort requests for properties that are not declared sortable, avoiding avoidable backend rejections in object exploration flows.
bdd_acceptance: Given detailed property metadata marks `summary` as not sortable, When the Browser table renders, Then the `summary` column is not exposed as a sortable header.
Given detailed property metadata marks `deliveredDate` as sortable, When the user sorts that column, Then the Browser request includes `orderBy` for `deliveredDate`.
Given detailed property metadata is still loading or unavailable, When the table renders, Then only the primary key sort affordance remains enabled rather than assuming every property is sortable.
